- If sentiment shows strong negative or positive bias in recent days, adjust forecast to reflect sentiment-driven mean reversion or reversal, especially if price has recently spiked.
- Avoid linear extrapolation after sharp spikes; reduce forecast slope after price surges (e.g., >70% from prior day) to prevent overshoot.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), reduce forecast slope for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment history includes alternating +1 and -1, model should not assume consistent trend; apply smoothing or volatility dampening.
- If forecast consistently overestimates true outcome by >5% over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for next 3 days.
- If sentiment shows strong negative sentiment (e.g., -1.00) in last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows early decline, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, forecast should not be overly aggressive; use 1–2% conservative adjustment unless strong trend persists.
